title: Go: JSON Encoding and Decoding
description: Marshal and unmarshal JSON data with Go structs, tags, and nested types.

steps.title: Marshal a struct
steps.description: Define a `Person` struct with `Name` and `Age` fields. Create an instance and use `json.Marshal` to convert it to JSON. Print the JSON byte slice as a string.
hints: Struct fields must be exported (capitalized) for json.Marshal
Convert the result to string for printing: `fmt.Println(string(data))`

verification.failureMessage: Make sure the struct fields are exported (capitalized).

steps.title: Unmarshal JSON
steps.description: Take the JSON string `{"Name":"Alice","Age":30}` and use `json.Unmarshal` to decode it into a `Person` struct. Print the Name and Age fields individually.
hints: `json.Unmarshal([]byte(jsonStr), &p)` — pass a pointer to the struct
Create a var `var p Person` to hold the result

verification.successMessage: JSON decoded back into a Go struct!
verification.failureMessage: Remember to pass a pointer to Unmarshal.

steps.title: MarshalIndent
steps.description: Marshal the same Person struct using `json.MarshalIndent` with a prefix of "" and indent of "  " (two spaces). Print the prettified JSON.
hints: The output should have line breaks and indentation

verification.successMessage: Indented JSON looks clean and readable!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure you use MarshalIndent with spaces as the indent string.

steps.title: Custom field names with tags
steps.description: Define a `User` struct with JSON tags: `Username string \`json:"username"\`` and `Email string \`json:"email,omitempty"\``. Marshal and show the output uses lowercase keys.
hints: JSON tags let you control the key names in the output
`omitempty` omits the field if it's the zero value
Tags go after the field type in backticks

verification.successMessage: Custom JSON tags control field naming!
verification.failureMessage: The JSON output should show lowercase keys, not the Go field names.

steps.title: Nested JSON
steps.description: Define an `Address` struct (Street, City) and a `Company` struct (Name, Address). Marshal a Company instance and print the nested JSON.
hints: Embed the Address struct as a field in Company
The JSON output will be nested: `{"Name":...,"Address":{"Street":...,"City":...}}`

verification.failureMessage: Make sure the Address field in Company is exported.
